chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Bakr, do you know how many Takbiirs are in the Salat upon the deceased?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Five Takbiirs.' Then he said: 'Do you know from where the five have been taken?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The five Takbiirs have been taken from the five (daily) Salats; from each Salat is one Takbeer.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the number of Takbiirs in the Shia funeral prayer and what is its scriptural or analogical basis?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential basis for the five Takbiirs in Salat al-Mayyit, attributing the number to a symbolic correspondence with the five daily prayers rather than a direct prophetic tradition. In Shia scholarship, this analogy (qiyas) highlights the structural symmetry between the deceased's final journey and the living's daily worship, reinforcing the ritual's spiritual continuity. The narration underscores the Imam's role in clarifying legal nuances that may not be explicitly detailed in the Quran.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Usman Bin Abdul Malik Al Hazramy, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘O Abu Bakr! Do you know how is the Salaat upon the deceased?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘Five exclamations of Takbeer. So, do you know where the five have been taken from?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘The five Takbeers have been taken from the five (daily) Salaats, from each Salaat being one Takbeer’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Abd al-Malik al- Hadramiy from abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked, ‘O abu Bakr, do you know how much is Salah (prayer) for a deceased?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is five Takbir (Allah is great beyond description). Do you know from where are they taken?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Five Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) are taken from five Salah (prayer), one Takbir from every Salah (prayer).”’
